entries.argument: The live biographies identify two distinct adult Larne men: James Glasgow-1509, ropemaker (1737–1802), and James Glasgow-3991, probable tanner (about 1748–1812). == Biography ==
'''James Glasgow''' was reportedly born in '''1737'''. A Larne or Kilwaughter congregational record is said to contain an entry for a James, son of [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]], at '''New Town, Larne''', in that year.

The original congregational entry, or a reliable full transcription, has not yet been cited on this profile. The exact birth date, place and identification of Hugh as James’s father should therefore be treated as probable rather than conclusively established.

James was a '''ropemaker''' at Larne, County Antrim. A lease dated 10 September 1760, registered on 24 November 1763, describes him as a ropemaker of Belfast and leases him a marked-out ropewalk at Gardenmore in Larne for thirty-one years from 1 November 1760. He agreed to build a house at the south end of the ropewalk.<ref name="Ropewalk1760">Registry of Deeds transcript, lease dated 10 September 1760 and registered 24 November 1763, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-S7XZ-8 FamilySearch image].</ref>

On 28 March 1768 James, described as a ropemaker of the Old Town of Larne, assigned the plot, workhouse and remainder of the same lease to John Hill for £50. The matching commencement date and rent identify it as the 1760 ropewalk.<ref name=

[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

'''James Glasgow''' was born about 1748, the son of '''[[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]]''' and his wife '''[[Unknown-763010|Ann Glasgow]]'''. His approximate year of birth is calculated from his age at death.<ref name="Armorial">"Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim," ''Ulster Journal of Archaeology'', second series 6 (1900), [https://archive.org/details/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/page/47/mode/1up p. 47], Glasgow monument inscription.</ref>

The family monument explicitly identifies James as the son of Hugh and Ann Glasgow. Hugh died on 8 July 1767, aged 62, and Ann died on 8 June 1786, aged 75.<ref name="Armorial" />

James married '''[[Unknown-763421|Jane]]''', whose maiden name is not given in the monument inscription. Jane was born about 1741, based on her recorded age at death.<ref name="Armorial" />

James and Jane had at least one known child:

* '''[[Glasgow-3992|Ann Glasgow]]''', born about 1768; died 25 May 1832, aged 64.<ref name="Armorial" />

James died on '''14 April 1812''', aged 64.<ref name="Armorial" /> His stated age places his birth approximately between 15 April 1747 and 14 April 1748.

His wife Jane survived him. She died on '''21 July 1820''', aged 79.<ref name="Armorial" />
